text:
asha: heads up — a bunch of inference pods (edge region eu-west-3) using the headless service llm-worker-headless can't resolve peer IPs across nodes. Started after we scaled GPU nodepool + bumped kubelet kube-proxy on those nodes.

martin: :eyes: seeing the same from prometheus: pod-to-pod latency spikes and a lot of `no endpoints` errors in the app logs. Are endpointSlices being created?

asha: checked quickly — endpointSlices exist but often have empty endpoints array for that service on several nodes. Only shows up after node restart.

julie: cluster-monitor alert fired: `EndpointSliceController high API retries` around the same time. Maybe controller-manager overloaded when the GPU nodes joined.

ryan: could also be kube-proxy mode? We're running iptables on those edge nodes because of older kernel. iptables conntrack + NAT at the edge NAT gateway might be dropping intra-cluster traffic.

asha: ran these to inspect:
```
kubectl -n inference get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=llm-worker-headless -o wide
kubectl -n inference describe svc llm-worker-headless
kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/coredns
```
Logs show a lot of SERVFAILs for headless lookups and coredns complaining about upstream timeouts to the cluster DNS forwarders.

martin: interesting — headless means DNS returns A records directly from endpoints. If endpointSlices are empty, DNS will return nothing. Two possible root causes: endpoint controller failing to populate slices, or kubelet/node agents not reporting podIPs to apiserver.

julie: can we check kubelet registration on the GPU nodes? Maybe they have flakey network to the control plane because of egress NAT limits in that edge region.

asha: ran `kubectl get nodes -o wide` — GPU nodes show Ready but kubelet version report is delayed in node status sometimes. Also saw a handful of 'eviction' events earlier when disk pressure flared during model downloads.

ryan: eviction events could lead to pods restarting and endpoint controller thrashing. Also if node's kube-proxy can't program rules due to iptables rate limits, endpoints won't get routed properly.

cluster-monitor: EVENT: controller-manager pod restart count increased (3x) in last 10m; API server 429s observed. Suggest pausing node-provisioning.

martin: temporary mitigation ideas: 1) cordon new GPU nodes that were joining-pending, 2) scale up controller-manager (if self-hosted) or open ticket with managed control plane, 3) toggle kube-proxy to ipvs on affected nodes (longer change), 4) reduce model prefetch parallelism to avoid disk pressure.

julie: quick patch we pushed: drained two of the newest GPU nodes and restarted kube-proxy on one. EndpointSlices repopulated for llm-worker-headless immediately after restart on that node. DNS lookups started resolving across nodes again.

asha: confirmed: after drain+restart, coredns SERVFAILs dropped and app saw steady peer discovery. But still seeing occasional empty EndpointSlice entries for a subset of nodes.

ryan: followups:
- increase controller-manager CPU/memory (or ask managed CP to investigate API throttling)
- add healthcheck to node provisioning job to wait for kube-proxy and kubelet readiness before marking node available
- add extra conntrack table size on edge NAT gateway and tune iptables nf_conntrack_max on GPU nodes
- consider route-based egress (no NAT) for intra-cluster traffic in edge regions to avoid masquerade issues

martin: +1 on conntrack tuning. Also add a short-term probe to reconcile EndpointSlices more aggressively for headless services with critical workloads (inference).

ops-bot: note added to incident timeline: `1745009876 - headless DNS / endpointSlice instability in eu-west-3; mitigation: drained new GPU nodes, restarted kube-proxy; followups created` :white_check_mark:

julie: I'll open PR with the kube-proxy restart playbook and add conntrack sysctl defaults for the edge image. Also filing a ticket with infra to check NAT gateway scaling limits.

asha: thanks — leaving the thread open while we monitor. If anyone sees a reoccurrence, ping here with `kubectl get endpointslices -n inference -l kubernetes.io/service-name=llm-worker-headless -o json | jq '.items[] | {nodePorts: .ports, endpoints: .endpoints|length}'` results.
